title: Fire Config
description: JSON Schema for authoring and validating Fire configuration files.

dir.description: Project working directory. Defaults to '.'. Use null to run from the current process directory.

group.description: File-level group used as a command prefix for all commands in this file. If omitted, the group is inferred from the filename (e.g. tracking.fire.yml -> 'tracking'; the base fire.yml/fire.yaml files never infer a group). Use null to keep the file ungrouped.

description.description: Optional file-level description. When `group` is set, this description is shown for that group in help and completion.

env_file.description: Environment file(s) for this Fire file. null disables automatic .env loading.

environment.description: Inline environment values for this Fire file.

runtimes.description: Runtime definitions keyed by alias (for example: deno, py).

shell.description: File-level default for `shell` on every command in this file. Interpreter for every shell snippet of the command: `exec`, shell `compute`, `before` and `check`; the `runner`, and a runtime's `runner` and `check`, are also launched through it (`<shell> -c '<runner>'`). Defaults to `sh`. Accepts any executable with optional arguments (`zsh`, `/bin/bash -l`) or a variable such as `$SHELL` for the user's login shell. Non-interactive shells don't load `.zshrc`/`.bashrc`, so aliases and functions defined there aren't available.

session.description: File-level default for `session` on every command in this file. Set to false to run the command directly, never inside a session. By default, in a terminal every fire command runs in a session on a pty that you can detach (Ctrl+Z) and reattach (`fg`, or `fire cli fg <id>` from anywhere). Use it for programs that misbehave under the supervisor.

long_running.description: File-level default for `long_running` on every command in this file. Marks servers, watchers and workers. Without a terminal (agents' shells, scripts) the command starts as a detached session, prints its id and returns right away instead of blocking; an identical running session is reused. In a terminal it changes nothing. The MCP server exposes it so agents use `start_session`.

include.description: List of additional local directories (relative to current directory) where Fire should load fire config files. Search is direct-level only (non-recursive).

commands.description: Command definitions keyed by command name. The top-level command name `cli` is reserved and cannot be defined (validation error example: 'Property cli is not allowed.').

cli.description: Reserved command name. `commands.cli` is not allowed at the top level because `cli` is used internally by Fire.

containerRunner.description: Container object: fire only generates a string runner from it, `<engine> run --rm -i [-t] <flags> <image> [command]`, which is what it runs, logs and shows in `--dry-run`. Keys follow Docker Compose. Values you write go into the string as written (the shell expands `$VAR`, `~`, `$(...)`); paths fire computes are quoted.

engine.description: Container engine. Only the host alias for runtimes differs (`host.docker.internal` / `host.containers.internal`).

tty.description: Adds `-t`. Never inferred from the terminal. In a command runner it needs `{fire.exec}` in `command`, since otherwise the commands go to stdin, which can't be a terminal.

command.description: What runs inside the image. Command runners: when omitted, the image's own command runs and fire writes the commands to its stdin (works for images whose default is a shell, like `alpine`); for others write `sh -c {fire.exec}` or `sh`. Runtime runners: defaults to the sdk's executable and must end in it.

volumes.description: `host:container[:options]` mounts. Relative host paths (`./`, `../`) resolve from the fire file's directory. When set, they REPLACE the inferred mounts entirely (the project directory, the command's `dir` and the runtime `paths` directories, at the same absolute path): mount them yourself if you still need them.

working_dir.description: `-w` inside the container. Defaults to the command's resolved `dir`.

environment.description: Extra variables for the container, on top of the command's `environment`/`env_file` (these win on conflict). Fire passes every variable as `-e NAME` and sets the value in the runner's environment, so values never appear in the log or `--dry-run`. The host environment is not passed.

user.description: `--user`. No default. On Linux, `$(id -u):$(id -g)` keeps files written to the mounted project owned by you.

network_mode.description: `--network <mode>`, as in Compose. With `host`, runtimes reach fire at `127.0.0.1` (needed with native Docker on Linux); otherwise through the engine's host alias.

args.description: Extra flags for `run`, added as written before the image.

prefix.description: Namespace prefix used in CLI paths.

sdk.description: Runtime SDK identifier used in runtime expressions.

oneOf.description: The sdk's executable, or a command that ends in it (`deno`, `uv run python`, `docker run --rm -i denoland/deno:latest`). Fire appends the sdk's bootstrap arguments and never rewrites it. Launched through the command's `shell`. Fire exports `FIRE_RUNTIME_RPC_ADDR` and `FIRE_RUNTIME_RPC_PORT`; a container runner must pass the address itself, e.g. `-e FIRE_RUNTIME_RPC_ADDR=host.docker.internal:$FIRE_RUNTIME_RPC_PORT` (Docker Desktop) or `--network host -e FIRE_RUNTIME_RPC_ADDR=127.0.0.1:$FIRE_RUNTIME_RPC_PORT` (native Docker on Linux).

runner.description: The sdk's executable or a command that ends in it, or a container object that fire turns into one (default `command`: the sdk's executable; fire adds the RPC address).

check.description: Health-check command to verify runtime availability.

fallback_runner.description: Runner used when `check` fails. Same rule as `runner`: the sdk's executable, or a command that ends in it, or a container object.

paths.description: Glob patterns where runtime scripts/functions are discovered.

stringOrStringArray.description: A single command string or a sequence of command strings.

commandEntry.description: Command shorthand string or full command object.

<<.description: YAML merge key used to reuse anchored blocks.

dir.description: Command-specific working directory. Overrides top-level `dir`; null runs from the current process directory.

check.description: Pre-check command; can be paired with `fallback_runner`.

shell.description: Interpreter for every shell snippet of the command: `exec`, shell `compute`, `before` and `check`; the `runner`, and a runtime's `runner` and `check`, are also launched through it (`<shell> -c '<runner>'`). Defaults to `sh`. Accepts any executable with optional arguments (`zsh`, `/bin/bash -l`) or a variable such as `$SHELL` for the user's login shell. Non-interactive shells don't load `.zshrc`/`.bashrc`, so aliases and functions defined there aren't available.

runner.description: Command that runs `exec` inside another environment (container, ssh, ...), exactly as written, or a container object that fire turns into such a command. With `{fire.exec}` in it, fire replaces it with the commands as one quoted argument and stdin stays free (`docker run --rm -it node sh -c {fire.exec}`); don't quote it yourself. Without it, the commands are written to the runner's stdin, so it needs `-i` and no `-t` (`docker run --rm -i node sh`). Launched through `shell`.

fallback_runner.description: Runner used if `check` fails. Same rules as `runner`: `{fire.exec}` or commands on stdin, or a container object.

before.description: Command executed before the main action.

needs.description: Whitespace-separated Fire command paths in this file's scope that must complete first. Each dependency runs once per invocation, receives no user arguments, and runs before `before`. Long-running commands are not allowed.

parallel.description: Run this command's `needs` concurrently. Output is prefixed by command path and the first failure cancels the rest.

description.description: Short user-facing description shown in listings and completion.

driver.description: External CLI executable name. Fire forwards every remaining argument exactly as a separate OS argument. Install a repository with `fire cli driver install <github-repo-url>` to delegate completion through its `driver.yaml`.

session.description: Set to false to run the command directly, never inside a session. By default, in a terminal every fire command runs in a session on a pty that you can detach (Ctrl+Z) and reattach (`fg`, or `fire cli fg <id>` from anywhere). Use it for programs that misbehave under the supervisor.

long_running.description: Marks servers, watchers and workers. Without a terminal (agents' shells, scripts) the command starts as a detached session, prints its id and returns right away instead of blocking; an identical running session is reused. In a terminal it changes nothing. The MCP server exposes it so agents use `start_session`.

agents.description: Set to false to keep this command, and every subcommand under it, away from agents: the MCP server does not list it and `start_session` refuses to run it. Help marks it as `[no agents]`. This guides well-behaved agents; to hard-block an agent's shell, also add a deny rule in your agent's permissions.

on_unused_args.description: Behavior for unused args at this command level.

env_file.description: Environment file(s) for this command. Replaces the file-level setting; null disables loading.

environment.description: Inline environment values for this command. Replaces the file-level map.

exec.description: Shell command(s) to execute. If an array is provided, commands run in order.

eval.description: Runtime expression(s) to evaluate (for example: py:func("{1}")).

compute.description: Computed variables map (name -> expression), evaluated before execution. If expression uses a known runtime prefix (<runtime>:<code>) it is evaluated in that runtime; otherwise it is executed as a shell command.

macros.description: Macro substitutions map used in `exec` and nested command strings.

commands.description: Nested subcommands keyed by subcommand name.
